claims.text: Concentration-dependent bactericidal: inhibit DNA gyrase and topoisomerase (bacterial DNA replication).
claims.quote: Fluoroquinolones exhibit concentration-dependent bactericidal activity by inhibiting the activity of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase, enzymes essential for bacterial DNA replication.

claims.text: Boxed warning: disabling, possibly irreversible tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, myasthenia gravis exacerbation; stop at once if they occur.
claims.quote: Fluoroquinolones, including levofloxacin, have been associated with disabling and potentially irreversible serious adverse reactions that have occurred together [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )], including: o Tendinitis and tendon rupture [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )] o Peripheral neuropathy [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )] o Central nervous system effects [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.4 )] Discontinue levofloxacin immediately

claims.text: Also QT prolongation,
claims.quote: QT-interval prolongation can occur, potentially leading to ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

claims.text: aortic aneurysm/dissection,
claims.quote: Aortic aneurysm and dissection can occur

claims.text: hypo/hyperglycemia (usually diabetics on insulin or oral agents),
claims.quote: Fluoroquinolones, including levofloxacin, have been associated with disturbances of blood glucose, including symptomatic hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, usually in diabetic patients receiving concomitant treatment with an oral hypoglycemic agent (e.g., glyburide) or with insulin.

claims.text: C. difficile diarrhea,
claims.quote: Clostridioides (formerly Clostridium) difficile–associated diarrhea (pseudomembranous colitis) has been strongly associated with fluoroquinolone use

claims.text: photosensitivity.
claims.quote: Moderate to severe photosensitivity/phototoxicity reactions

claims.text: Prior allergy; arrhythmia-prone states (QT prolongation, uncorrected hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia, significant bradycardia) or other QT-prolonging drugs.
claims.quote: Contraindications include - Previous allergic reaction to the medications - Certain disorders that predispose to arrhythmias (eg, QT-interval prolongation, uncorrected hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia, significant bradycardia) - Use of medications known to prolong the QT interval or to cause bradycardia

claims.text: Avoid in myasthenia gravis,
claims.quote: Muscle weakness may be exacerbated in patients with myasthenia gravis, so fluoroquinolones should be avoided in these patients.

claims.text: CNS disorders,
claims.quote: Seizures are rare, but fluoroquinolones should not be used in patients with CNS disorders.

claims.text: and known aortic aneurysm or its risk factors (eg, Marfan).
claims.quote: Aortic aneurysm and dissection can occur, with a potentially increased risk in patients who have risk factors for aortic aneurysm (eg, Marfan syndrome) or who have a known aortic aneurysm.

claims.text: Children: AAP advises second-line use only, in a few situations with no reasonable alternative.
claims.quote: many experts, including the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), challenge this view because evidence is weak, and they recommend prescribing fluoroquinolones as a second-line antibiotic and restricting use to a few specific situations when there are no reasonable alternatives

claims.text: Pregnancy: only if benefit exceeds risk and no safer alternative.
claims.quote: Fluoroquinolones should be used in pregnancy only if clinical benefit exceeds risk and a safer alternative is not available.
claims.locator: Use of Fluoroquinolones During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Ciprofloxacin + tizanidine contraindicated.
claims.quote: Concomitant administration with tizanidine is contraindicated

claims.text: Polyvalent cations (Al, Mg, Ca, Zn, iron) cut oral absorption:
claims.quote: Oral absorption is diminished by coadministration of polyvalent cations (aluminum, magnesium, calcium, zinc, and iron preparations).

claims.text: give levofloxacin at least two hours before or after antacids, sucralfate, iron, zinc multivitamins.
claims.quote: Levofloxacin tablets should be administered at least two hours before or two hours after antacids containing magnesium, aluminum, as well as sucralfate, metal cations such as iron, and multivitamin preparations with zinc

claims.text: Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels
claims.quote: Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels, sometimes resulting in theophylline-related adverse effects.

claims.text: (serious and fatal reactions reported).
claims.quote: Serious and fatal reactions have been reported in patients receiving concurrent administration of ciprofloxacin and theophylline.
claims.locator: 5.10 Serious Adverse Reactions with Concomitant Theophylline

claims.text: Avoid excessive sun/UV exposure; stop if phototoxicity occurs.
claims.quote: Therefore, excessive exposure to these sources of light should be avoided. Drug therapy should be discontinued if photosensitivity/phototoxicity occurs

claims.text: Diabetics: monitor glucose; stop if hypoglycemia occurs.
claims.quote: In these patients, careful monitoring of blood glucose is recommended. Severe cases of hypoglycemia resulting in coma or death have been reported. If a hypoglycemic reaction occurs in a patient being treated with levofloxacin, discontinue levofloxacin
